analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is a captive wind O&M services arm with ₹236 Cr revenue, near-zero returns (ROE 1%), and negative 7-year revenue CAGR (-6.1%) trading at an absurd 81x P/E and 129x EV/EBITDA. The clean balance sheet was achieved via massive equity dilution — not earnings power — making this a value trap dressed in renewable energy clothing.
key_strengths: Debt virtually eliminated (₹1,411 Cr in 2021 → ₹95 Cr in 2025), D/E now just 0.05
Structural tailwind: India's wind energy capacity expansion drives O&M demand
Promoter holding stable at 56% with parent Inox Wind providing captive order flow
key_risks: Valuation is disconnected from reality: 81x P/E and 129x EV/EBITDA on barely profitable business earning ₹22 Cr net profit
Revenue has gone nowhere in 7 years — ₹368 Cr in 2018, ₹236 Cr in 2025 (-6.1% CAGR); O&M contract growth has not materialised
Equity base exploded from ₹43 Cr (2021) to ₹2,020 Cr (2025) — debt was cleaned via shareholder dilution, not operating cash generation
red_flags: Captive subsidiary of Inox Wind — related-party concentration risk with no independent growth engine
Operating CF turned positive only recently (₹60 Cr in FY25) but investing CF hit -₹637 Cr — capital being deployed at near-zero ROCE of 2.6%
Net profit declining: ₹28 Cr in FY2024 → ₹22 Cr in FY2025, even as 'Other Income' jumped to ₹57 Cr (non-operating crutch)
Market cap of ₹6,549 Cr on ₹236 Cr revenue = 22x P/S for a services business with no pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, this business fails the most basic test I apply before writing a cheque: can the company earn a decent return on the capital employed? ROE of 1% and ROCE of 2.6% are worse than a fixed deposit. The company raised roughly ₹1,500+ Cr of fresh equity since 2021 purely to retire debt inherited from prior years of losses — that's not value creation, that's dilution-as-survival. Revenue at ₹236 Cr in FY2025 is actually lower than the ₹368 Cr in 2018, meaning seven years of India's wind boom passed without this company compounding its own topline. I want businesses growing 15-20% annually; this one is shrinking in real terms.

The valuation is nothing short of speculative excess. At 81x P/E on ₹22 Cr of declining profits — with ₹57 Cr of "Other Income" doing the heavy lifting — this stock is priced for perfection that the business has never demonstrated. India's renewable energy story is absolutely real and I believe in it deeply, but the right way to play it is not through a captive O&M subsidiary with broken unit economics. The wind O&M market is competitive, margins are under pressure (EBITDA contracting 5-year trend), and being effectively locked to parent Inox Wind's installed base limits the addressable opportunity. Avoid completely at current prices.
